name: Ānāpānasati (breath meditation, "Method 2")
howto: Sit upright and notice the breath at whatever point it is clearest. Let it settle into a comfortable rhythm, then let that sense of ease spread through the whole body, using the breath energy as a home base for steady, alert attention.

name: "Buddho" recollection
howto: Silently repeat "bud-" on the in-breath and "-dho" on the out-breath to anchor the mind; when the mind is calm, drop the word and stay with the knowing itself. Used widely in the Ajahn Mun and Ajahn Chah lines.

name: Walking meditation (jongrom)
howto: Choose a straight path of 15–30 paces. Walk at a natural or slow pace, attention on the feet or the whole body; at each end, stop, turn, and re-collect before walking back.

name: Mettā (loving-kindness)
howto: Wish well to yourself, then a benefactor, a friend, a neutral person, a difficult person and finally all beings, using simple phrases or a felt sense of goodwill, letting it spread in every direction.

name: Mahasi noting
howto: Watch the rise and fall of the abdomen and give each event a soft mental label ("rising", "falling", "thinking", "hearing"), then return to the primary object; move to slow walking with labels for lifting, moving and placing.

name: Body sweeping (Goenka vipassanā)
howto: After a few days of ānāpāna to sharpen attention, move attention systematically through the body from head to feet, observing every sensation with equanimity, as taught in ten-day residential courses.

name: Natural awareness (right attitude)
howto: Instead of forcing focus on one object, relax and know whatever is being experienced, checking the attitude of the observing mind (craving, aversion, impatience) throughout daily activities.

name: Satipaṭṭhāna (four establishings of mindfulness)
howto: Contemplate body, feeling, mind and mental qualities as they arise and pass, ardent, clearly knowing and mindful, without greed or distress about the world (MN 10).

name: RAIN
howto: Recognise what is happening; Allow it to be there; Investigate with kindness how it feels in the body; Nurture with self-compassion; then rest in the awareness that remains.

name: Śravaṇa–manana–nididhyāsana
howto: Systematic listening to the Upaniṣads with a teacher (śravaṇa), resolving doubts by reflection (manana), and dwelling on the understood meaning until it is assimilated (nididhyāsana).

name: Japa (repetition of a divine name)
howto: Repeat a mantra or name of God given by the teacher, often with a mālā of 108 beads, letting the mind rest in its meaning and the feeling of devotion.

name: Hare Krishna mahāmantra (japa and kīrtan)
howto: Chant "Hare Kṛṣṇa Hare Kṛṣṇa, Kṛṣṇa Kṛṣṇa Hare Hare / Hare Rāma Hare Rāma, Rāma Rāma Hare Hare" softly on beads (japa) or sing it together (kīrtan), as practised since Chaitanya.

name: Yoga nidrā
howto: Lying down, rotate awareness through the body, then breath, opposite sensations and visualisations while staying awake, ending with a personal resolve (saṅkalpa).

name: Five points of yoga (Sivananda)
howto: Proper exercise (āsana), proper breathing (prāṇāyāma), proper relaxation, proper diet and positive thinking with meditation, as summarised by Swami Vishnudevananda.

name: Breath-centred, individually adapted āsana (viniyoga)
howto: Link every movement to a slow inhale or exhale and adapt sequence, length and intensity to the person's body, age and aims, as taught by Krishnamacharya and T. K. V. Desikachar.
